finalists.why: Best overall in the composite score (3.3). Its band shape is closest to the reference (2.9 dB RMS distance; every other candidate is 3.6 dB or more). It has the second-lowest tonal ratio (15.5 dB, ref 16.7) and crest 24.4 dB (ref 25.1). Its -30/-40 dB tail is noise, not ring: tail tonality is 16.8 dB, the second-lowest. Its sweep has the cleanest reading in the field (ratchet/fidget, glitch only +2.43) and a gentle spectrum (2-5 kHz share -9.1 dB). One weakness: 'an error buzz' +2.5 is third in the tick readings.

finalists.name: felt-dome
finalists.title: Felt

finalists.why: Earshot hears it as the closest to the reference (CLAP cosine 0.69). Its crest matches the reference (25.0 vs 25.1 dB), and it has the second-softest attack (3.2 ms) and the lowest local tonal prominence in the field (7.0 dB, so no ring). The global tonal ratio of 21.6 dB comes from its darker slope. The tick reads cleanly (1% bad terms in forced choice). Level is capped at 1.0: its sweep measures -41.7 LUFS, 0.4 dB under the target, which is inside the 0.5 dB tolerance. Weaknesses: the sweep reads 'digital glitch' +2.93 with 'error buzz' +2.40, and the tick has 'an error buzz' +2.53 in its top 3.

finalists.name: breath-feather
finalists.title: Feather

This is the strongest ratchet reading of any sweep, the closest to a rotary dial returning.
finalists.why: It is the softest by the model-free numbers: the lowest tonal ratio of all 12 (12.6 dB, below the ref's 16.7), the softest attack (3.5 ms), and the most noise-like tail (tail tonality 12.2 dB). Its centroid matches the reference's (7.9 vs 7.8 kHz). Its sweep reads as ratchet/fidget clicking and stays gentle (2-5 kHz share -8.0 dB). Caveat: it is a sibling of Hush (waveform xcorr 0.71). It is kept as the airier, brighter alternative, but the two may sound alike. The tick also has 'an error buzz' +2.58 in its top 3.

finalists.why: It has the cleanest single-tick reading in the field and the strongest key-release match (z +3.56). It is the driest tick: falls of 6/10/12 ms, and only -30.5 dB of energy after 8 ms, so there is no tail anyone could hear as echo. Its sweep has the least energy in the harsh 2-5 kHz band of any candidate (-13.0 dB, the same as the ref sweep's -12.7; the current Dial's is -2.4). It is the only tock that survives. Weaknesses: its sweep has the highest glitch reading of all (stutter glitch +3.37), probably because of its very dry clicks with digital silence between them. It is also brighter than the ref and has no low end.

method:
1) Reproduction. I re-rendered all 12 recipes with softlib.write and sweep.write_sweep into judge/. Every tick and every sweep matches the designer's WAV sample for sample (np.array_equal). Every recipe uses only the softlib keys: length, seed, level, post_lowpass and calls of strike/thump with documented parameters. I re-measured all metrics with metrics.py, and the claimed numbers reproduced exactly.
2) Listening. ONE earshot process (EARSHOT_THREADS=2, about 20 s) ran describe on every tick, every sweep, the ref, the ref sweep, the current Dial and its sweep. It also ran match(tick, 'a soft key release click') with 15 alts, ab(ref, tick, query) for every tick, and api.measure on every sweep. The alts include 'a single mechanical keyboard key press', which takes much of the forced-choice share. That is why my key-release percentages are lower than the designers' claims (for example breath-hush 30% here vs 87% claimed); the bad-term shares are comparable.
3) Originality. I computed the max normalised cross-correlation of each tick with ref.wav. All are between 0.20 and 0.34, below the 0.5 threshold, so none is suspicious. Between candidates, breath-hush and breath-feather are 0.71, the rest at most 0.46.
4) Ranking. I averaged per-criterion ranks into four groups:
- softness: tonal ratio, attack, crest.
- earshot cleanliness: worst bad-term z in the tick's top 5, forced-choice share of glitch/buzz/beep/kick/kalimba/triangle/bell/ding/glass/water, key-release z.
- sweep gentleness: worst bad-term z in the sweep's top 5, and the sweep's 2-5 kHz energy share.
- closeness to the ref: CLAP cosine from ab, and RMS distance of the six band shares.
Extra model-free checks: local tonal prominence over 1/3 octave, energy after 8 ms and its tonality, and the momentary-loudness maximum of each levelled sweep. After levelling, every sweep's momentary maximum is -37.1 to -37.8 LUFS (ref -37.6), so none builds up harshly. No candidate rings like the Dial (Dial: tonal 31.9 dB, -30 dB fall at 44 ms; every candidate's -30 dB fall is 26 ms or less).
Composite order: hush 3.3, dome 4.8, feather 5.2, air 5.8, puff 6.0, felt-hush 6.1, pad 6.3, pawl 7.6, round 7.9, settle 8.0, wood 8.1, housing 8.3. I swapped puff for pad because puff's sweep reads glitch/zipper and pad adds the dark end of the range.
5) Loudness. The target is the ref's own samples through sweep.sweep, measured by api.measure: -41.3 LUFS (the current Dial's sweep is -33.7). For each candidate, level = min(1, 10^((target - LUFS at level 1)/20)). I rendered each sweep at that level and measured it again: all reach -41.3, except felt-dome, which is capped at level 1.0 and measures -41.7 (0.4 dB under, inside the 0.5 dB tolerance).
